text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German debt prices were knocked off their pedestal late on Wednesday as stronger than expected U.S. industry output data sent U.S. Treasuries skidding down. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.66, down 0.21 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended slightly in the red on Wednesday, giving up early gains as Bunds and T-bonds backtracked. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-22/32, down 02/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures finished MATIF pit-trading flat on Wednesday after an early technical push fizzled out and the consequent retreat was accentuated after strong U.S. industrial production aUSIP data. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.04 up 0.02 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures closed down but above session lows in the wake of a fall in T-bonds on strong U.S. manufacturing data, but traders said the session had been quiet with prices already lower in a correction to the rally of recent days. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.58 down 0.44 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were dropping after strong manufacturing data, analysts pointed to continued vigor in consumer demand. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-06/32, down 14/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.13 percent.

JAPAN - Short-covering propelled cash and futures JGBs higher by the close on Wednesday, breaking, though temporarily, a key chart resistance of 126.88. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.51, down 0.11 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary Eurobond market was quick to pick up on the improved sentiment in government bond markets, with brisk activity on Wednesday morning. A $250 million three-year deal from an IBM finance arm proved the session's biggest hit as the 15 basis points reoffer spread quickly tightened to 13/12 b.p.

A syndicate official at lead manager SBC Warburg said corporate paper was continuing to outperform in the three- to five-year area. That aside, IBM has been popular with European retail since returning to the dollar sector last July after a four-year gap.
